articles.title: Fifa accuses Uefa of 'smear campaign' against Infantino
articles.summary: The governing bodies have traded blows since Fifa president Gianni Infantino's scrapped plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors.
body: Last week European football's governing body filed legal papers in the US requesting disclosure of evidence and documents from Fifa as part of potential criminal claims in Switzerland.

In a dramatic escalation of the controversy, Uefa accused Infantino of "criminal mismanagement" and "a fraudulently off-market price promoted by [him] for his own benefit" over the now-shelved Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) scheme.
However, world governing body Fifa has now responded with a court filing lodged in the US - and seen by the BBC - requesting that a court "oppose" the application by the end of the month.

Fifa said it had "made clear" that the creation of FFE was "only a proposal", adding that it could have only proceeded on the condition that the majority of member associations supported it and "the relevant approvals of the Fifa Council".

articles.title: Vuelta a España: Jakob Omrzel grabs first Grand Tour stage win as Enric Mas extends lead
articles.summary: Slovenian wins stage 12 as Mas strengthens position. Tim Merlier claims stage two in Tour of Britain. Spain’s Enric Mas extended his overall lead in the Vuelta a España with a late attack on his rivals ⁠as Slovenia’s Jakob Omrzel won stage 12 to Calar Alto on Thursday.
body: Movistar rider Mas burst out of a chasing group including red jersey contenders Primoz ⁠Roglic and Felix Gall ⁠with around ​13km of the mountainous 166.6-km ride left and powered away. Roglic and Gall, who began the day second and third on general classification, could not ⁠respond as Mas finished 27 seconds clear of Roglic to strengthen his hold on the race.

Omrzel attacked from a whittled-down lead group on the final ascent ⁠to Calar Alto and kept the power down to cross the line almost two minutes clear of ​Urko Berrade with Santiago Buitrago third. Aged 20, ‌Omrzel is younger than Slovenian ‌great Tadej Pogacar was when he won his first Grand Tour stage.

Mas took over the leadership ‌when overwhelming favourite and clear race leader Pogacar crashed out on stage eight and on a baking hot day in southern Spain on Thursday, he put down a big statement of intent for the remaining stages. The Mallorcan now leads by one minute and 45 seconds from Roglic with Gall at 2:06.
Britain’s Oscar Onley was the biggest loser on the day in the battle for overall victory as a crash meant he finished more than two minutes behind Mas.

articles.title: Manchester City’s Vivianne Miedema could miss rest of year with knee injury
articles.summary: Arsenal poised to land PSG’s Élisa De Almeida. New United coach Olid promises attacking style. Manchester City could be without Vivianne Miedema for at least the rest of 2026, the Guardian understands, after the Netherlands forward sustained a knee injury.
body: According to multiple sources the injury is not an anterior cruciate ligament but is serious and there are fears she will not return until after the Women’s Super League’s winter break. A statement from the club on Tuesday said Miedema would miss the “start of the season”.

City are understood to have sought reinforcements in attacking midfield to cover for Miedema, who predominantly played as a No 10 for the WSL champions last term. The Paris Saint-Germain and Nigeria midfielder Jennifer Echegini and the Everton and Spain forward Ornella Vignola are players City are understood to have inquired about before the 11pm BST WSL transfer deadline. According to sources, PSG are not willing to sell Echegini.
Arsenal are expected to finalise the signing of the France defender Élisa De Almeida from PSG. The club are understood to have agreed a fee of just over £500,000 for the 28-year-old.

articles.title: Somerset cement advantage against Glamorgan
articles.summary: Tom Lammonby fell five short of a century as Somerset cement their advantage on the second day of their County Championship match against Glamorgan.
body: Tom Lammonby fell five short of a century as Somerset cemented their advantage on the second day of the County Championship match with Glamorgan.

The home side extended their first innings score from an overnight 92 without loss to 441 all out, Lammonby's 95 coming off 173 balls, while Josh Thomas contributed 59, James Rew 52 and Archie Vaughan a season's best 68. That meant a first innings lead of 247, despite Mason Crane's 4-95.
Glamorgan were left with six overs in the day to launch their second innings and closed on 30-1, Crane caught at silly point off the last ball of the day, bowled by Jack Leach.

Unbeaten on 46 overnight, Thomas moved to an attractive 86-ball fifty with 9 fours. He had helped Lammonby take the opening stand to 114 when chasing a very wide ball from Mir Hamza and edging to wicketkeeper Chris Cooke.

articles.title: Wong stars as England thump Ireland to seal series
articles.summary: Issy Wong's first international five-wicket haul leads England to a six-wicket win over Ireland and seals the three-match series with a game to spare.
body: England sealed a comfortable series win as they hammered Ireland by six wickets in a one-sided encounter in the second one-day international at Derby.

Fast bowler Issy Wong took 5-33 - her first international five-wicket haul - as Ireland were dissmissed for 165 before England cruised to their target in 23 overs to take the series with a match to spare.
Though England made light work of the chase, they were guilty of throwing away their wickets.
Openers Maia Bouchier and Sophia Dunkley, who starred in England's record-breaking chase in the opener at Leicester, started positively with a stand of 54 in seven overs.

articles.title: Swansea on the way to reviving style - Matos
articles.summary: Vitor Matos believes his Swansea City side are on the way to reviving the sort of stylish possession game which was key to the club's golden period in the Premier League.
body: Swansea are top of the early Championship table having banked 10 points from their first four league games.
The Swans host Wrexham in a mouthwatering Welsh derby on Saturday having produced one of the club's best performances in recent memory as they overcame Watford in midweek.

Head coach Matos believes his new-look team are moving towards playing the sort of eye-catching football Swansea became known for under the likes of Roberto Martinez, Brendan Rodgers and Michael Laudrup.
"Swansea always had a style. When you closed your eyes and you started thinking about Swansea and what that style is and what the DNA of the club is, you got some images in your mind," he said.

articles.title: 3 Must-Watch Matchups in the 2026 ACC/SEC Challenge
articles.summary: The ACC/SEC Challenge matchups have quickly become some of the most anticipated games on the college basketball calendar. This year’s slate once again features several high-profile programs going head-to-head in important early-season tests.
body: Despite losing their top scorer, Labaron Philon Jr., Alabama head coach Nate Oats has reloaded his roster by retaining key pieces and targeting the transfer portal. After testing NBA waters, Amari Allen felt it was best to return to Alabama. This is massive for the Crimson Tide as they return one of the nation’s better defenders. Allen was tasked with the toughest assignments game after game. The expectations will be high for him. This is similar to Philon Jr., who, in his first year, was great and turned into a phenomenal scorer. Philon led the Crimson Tide in scoring last season.

Alongside Allen’s return, Oats has also brought in a talented freshman class that could make an immediate impact for the Crimson Tide. The first of the group is five-star McDonald’s All-American Jaxon Richardson. The six-foot-six wing is known to be one of the most athletic and bouncy freshmen in the class. Richardson does a great job of running the floor, creating easy transition points for himself. This is a perfect match for Oats, who likes to play fast on offense.

articles.title: FIFA accuses UEFA of launching 'smear campaign' against Gianni Infantino
articles.summary: FIFA has accused European football’s governing body of launching a “smear campaign” against Gianni Infantino in a challenge to legal action over the aborted attempt to sell part of the World Cup to private investors.
body: UEFA has warned it is considering launching criminal proceedings against Mr Infantino in Switzerland, where FIFA has its headquarters, and has filed legal cases in American courts.

UEFA has filed legal cases in American courts seeking evidence relating to the controversial venture and warned it is considering launching criminal proceedings against Mr Infantino in Switzerland where FIFA has its headquarters.

FIFA has now filed a response in a New York court, saying: "While these applications are styled as legal pleadings with captions and docket numbers, they are little more than press releases in further support of UEFA's smear campaign against FIFA and its leadership."
UEFA is trying to oust Mr Infantino from power with a resignation or in the FIFA presidential election in March.

articles.title: Barcelona failed with late attempt to sign 20-year-old Spanish starlet for reserve team
articles.summary: According to AS, FC Barcelona failed with a late attempt in the summer transfer window to sign Andres Vallecillo from Racing Santander. The newly-promoted La Liga club stood firm when the Blaugrana made a late approach for the youngster, insisting that he could only leave if his release clause was…
body: The Catalan club were prepared to offer around €300,000 for the youngster, but Racing refused to negotiate and Barça ultimately turned to Stuttgart midfielder Mirza Catovic instead.
On 30 August, Barcelona made an approach for Vallecillo, a midfielder born in Santander in 2006 who has developed under Ezequiel Loza at Rayo Cantabria, the club’s reserve team.
The La Liga champions wanted the 20-year-old starlet to reinforce their reserve team, Barça Atletic.
As such, they were prepared to pay a fee of around €300,000, but Racing rejected the proposal outright. Their position was clear: the release clause had to be paid or there would be no deal.

articles.title: ‘Pretty special’: N.J.’s Michael Zheng wins 1st main-draw match at U.S. Open
articles.summary: NEW YORK -- A huge crowd encircled Court 10 at the U.S. Open on Wednesday afternoon for the match featuring New Jersey native and former Columbia University star Michael Zheng.
body: His former college teammates sat in the corner of the court wearing the light blue of Columbia and cheering on the two-time former NCAA singles champion from Montville, N.J.

Competing in his first ever main-draw match at the Grand Slam in the city where he played college tennis, Zheng defeated Hungary’s Fábián Marozsán, 6-4, 6-4, 6-2, to advance to the second round on Thursday.

Zheng closed it out with a forehand winner up the line for his first main-draw win at the Open. Zheng reached 124 mph on his serve and finished with 33 winners against 17 unforced errors. He won 36-of-39 points (92%) on his first serve and often followed it up with a big forehand.

“Yeah, [it was] very exciting, especially to win here in New York City,” said Zheng, who is now up to No. 96 in the Live Rankings. “I didn’t get the chance to play main draw, the past three years [I was] in qualifying so to do it in front of a lot of alums, a lot of my teammates came out to watch, so to do it in front of everyone was pretty special.”

articles.title: Penalised Antonelli to help Russell at Italian GP
articles.summary: Kimi Antonelli is ready to help Mercedes team-mate and title rival George Russell in qualifying at the Italian Grand Prix for a race the world championship leader will start at the back of the grid due to an engine penalty.
body: Italy's own Antonelli arrives at his home track of Monza knowing that his healthy points advantage is almost certain to be eaten into this weekend owing to the fact Mercedes are triggering a back-of-the-grid start for him by exceeding power-unit component limits on his car, a legacy of reliability issues from earlier in the season.
Russell and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton both trail Antonelli by 59 points while McLaren's Lando Norris, the winner of the last two races, is 83 points behind.

Given he already knows he will start at the back of the grid whatever result he achieves on Saturday, Antonelli is open to aiding Russell's qualifying session and bid for pole position by providing slipstream assistance to the sister Mercedes around F1's fastest track to provide a straight-line speed and lap-time boost.
"It has been discussed with the team," said Antonelli when asked about the tow in Thursday's Drivers' Press Conference.
